MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

Patient: [redacted name]
Sex: Female
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]

REFERRAL REASON
Diagnostic testing for Cystic Fibrosis or CFTR-related disease. Clinical suspicion of CFTR-related disorder based on presenting symptoms.

TEST PERFORMED
CFTR Gene Screening Panel
- Common pathogenic variant screening
- Intron 8 PolyT tract genotyping

METHODOLOGY
Genomic DNA was extracted from peripheral blood leukocytes. PCR-based screening was performed using a commercial CFTR gene screening kit designed to detect common pathogenic variants associated with Cystic Fibrosis. The panel includes analysis of the most frequent disease-causing variants in the CFTR gene as recommended by ACMG/ACOG guidelines, representing approximately 90% of CF alleles in the general Caucasian population. Additionally, genotyping of the Intron 8 PolyT tract was performed to assess the 5T, 7T, and 9T allele status.

RESULTS

CFTR VARIANT SCREENING:
No pathogenic variants detected in the following positions:
- F508del (c.1521_1523delCTT): Not detected
- G542X (c.1624G>T): Not detected
- G551D (c.1652G>A): Not detected
- W1282X (c.3846G>A): Not detected
- N1303K (c.3909C>G): Not detected
- R553X (c.1657C>T): Not detected
- R117H (c.350G>A): Not detected
- Additional variants in screening panel: Not detected

INTRON 8 POLYT TRACT GENOTYPING:
Allele 1: 7T
Allele 2: 9T
Genotype: 7T/9T

The 7T allele has a frequency of approximately 5-10% in the general population. When present with the R117H variant, it can be associated with CFTR-related disorders. However, in the absence of R117H, the 7T allele typically does not cause disease.

SUMMARY
No clearly pathogenic variants were detected in the CFTR gene using this screening method. The patient's Intron 8 PolyT tract genotype is 7T/9T. This genotype, in the absence of other CFTR variants, is not associated with classic Cystic Fibrosis or CFTR-related disease.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS
These results indicate a reduced likelihood of CFTR-related disease caused by common CFTR variants. However, this screening panel detects approximately 90% of CF alleles in the Caucasian population and 70-95% in other ethnic groups. Rare or population-specific variants would not be detected by this method.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. If strong clinical suspicion for CFTR-related disease remains, consider comprehensive CFTR panel testing including full gene sequencing and deletion/duplication analysis
2. Clinical correlation with sweat chloride testing and pulmonary function studies is recommended
3. Genetic counseling is available to discuss these results and implications for family members

TEST LIMITATIONS
This screening panel is designed to detect common CFTR variants and does not include full gene sequencing. Rare variants, deep intronic variants, and large deletions/duplications would not be detected. The analytical sensitivity of this assay is >99% for the variants tested. This test was developed and validated by [redacted location] Medical Center Molecular Genetics Laboratory.

Authorized by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director
